lines.en: Olivia, we have finished the B1 course! How do you feel?
lines.pt: Olivia, terminamos o curso B1! Como você se sente?

lines.en: Proud. I used to be afraid of speaking, but I have made a lot of progress.
lines.pt: Orgulhosa. Eu tinha medo de falar, mas fiz muito progresso.

lines.en: I remember that you told me that you would never speak in class.

lines.en: Yes, and now I have asked questions in every lesson.

lines.en: If you had more time, what would you study next?

lines.en: I would learn about English films. Could you tell me which one you recommend?

lines.en: A film that was made in Chicago would be good. Many were filmed here.
lines.pt: Um filme que foi feito em Chicago seria bom. Muitos foram filmados aqui.

lines.en: Great idea. The teacher said that we could borrow her list.
lines.pt: Ótima ideia. A professora disse que podemos pegar a lista dela emprestada.

lines.en: I wonder if she has already given it to the others.
lines.pt: Será que ela já deu a lista aos outros.

lines.en: I don’t know. Let’s ask her before the class ends.
lines.pt: Não sei. Vamos perguntar a ela antes de a aula acabar.

lines.en: Good. I am so happy that we have learned so much together!
lines.pt: Bom. Estou tão feliz por termos aprendido tanto juntas!

facts.big: I have… / I used to… / If I had…, I would…
facts.label: Revisão do B1
facts.sub: Você já sabe usar o present perfect, used to, o 2º condicional, o passivo, o discurso indireto e perguntas indiretas. Misture tudo para falar de você.

facts.label: Já fiz
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para o que mudou até agora: I have made a lot of progress. We have finished the course. Nunca use went; use gone.

facts.label: Eu costumava
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para o hábito antigo: I used to be afraid of speaking. Compare com o presente: now I can talk for minutes.

compare.ask: I used to be afraid, but I have made progress.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “eu tinha medo de falar, mas agora falo” com o imperfeito.
compare.tip: Diga: “I used to be afraid, but I have made progress.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use used to + verbo base para o hábito antigo e o present perfect para o que mudou até agora: I used to be afraid, but I have made progress.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: I used to be afraid, but I have made progress.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Looking back at B1 · 1/3
paragraphs: It is the last day of class in Chicago, and the sun shines on the lake. Bea and Nina sit at a long table in a classroom. Each student has a certificate on the desk. Bea’s goal was to finish the course with good marks. Nina is looking at her old notebook and smiling. They want to talk about the long road behind them.

“Nina, we have finished the B1 course! How do you feel?” says Bea. “Proud. I used to be afraid of speaking, but I have made a lot of progress.” says Nina. “I remember that you told me that you would never speak in class.” says Bea.
